chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed is His Name: 'Surely prayer is a timed ordinance upon the Believers.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It means obligatory, and does not mean a time of missing it. If that time passes and then he prays it, his prayer is not considered rendered. And had it been so, Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him) would have been destroyed when he prayed it outside its time. But rather, whenever he remembered it, he prayed it.'

He (the narrator) said, 'Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And whenever you are convinced or doubt regarding its time that you did not pray it, or within the time of its missing that you did not pray it, you pray it. So if you doubt after the time of missing has passed, an obstacle has entered, so there is no repetition upon you from doubt until you are convinced. So if you are convinced, then upon you is that you pray it in whatever state you were.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying a missed prayer if one is unsure whether it was already performed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the term 'timed ordinance' (kitaban mawqutan) in Surah An-Nisa denotes the establishment of the obligation within a specific window, rather than a strict deadline where missing the time causes invalidation, as evidenced by Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) who prayed late without his prayer being void. This hadith establishes the principle of 'Qada' (making up missed prayers) and distinguishes between doubt during the valid period and doubt after the time has fully passed, ensuring that uncertainty does not impose an undue burden of repetition until certainty of omission arises.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Al Fuzayl,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj, Blessed is Hisazwj Name [4:103] surely prayer is a timed ordinance upon the Believers. Heasws said: ‘It Means Obligatory and does not mean a time being missed out. When that timing is exceeded, then he prays, his Salāt would not happen to be rendered. And had it been for that, Suleymanas Bin Dawoodas would have been destroyed when heas prayed it during other than its time. But, when heas remembered it, prayed it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you are convinced or doubt with regards to its timing that you have not prayed it, or you are within a timing of it being missed out, that you did not pray it, pray it. So if you were to doubt after the expiry of the time of it being missed out on, so an obstacle has entered. Therefore there is no repeating upon you from a doubt until you are convinced. So if you are convinced, then upon you is that you pray it in whichever state you were’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who forgets to perform the morning Salah (prayer) until it is sunrise. He (the Imam) said, ’He performs it whenever he remembers. The Messenger of Allah remained sleeping during the time for the morning Salah (prayer) until sunrise, then he performed it Qada’ (compensatory prayer) when he woke up but moved away from his place, then performed Salah (prayer).’”
